newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bread wheat steadier but feed wheat eases.
newsitem.headline: German bread wheat steadier but feed wheat eases.

text.p: Nominal German wheat export prices were marked up this week as farmers in the north were still gathering the delayed harvest, brokers said on Wednesday.
They said support came from samples showing protein contents and Hagberg numbers were not exceptional although Schleswig-Holstein state reported reasonably good qualities.
They also cited latent storeholder demand and Polish demand for grain from Mecklenburg state on the German/Polish border.
"Milling industry buyers are still very passive but they have not complained about the higher levels," one broker said.
The Hamburg grain exchange raised its new crop bread wheat price (12.5 percent, 220 Hagberg) by 2.50 marks on the week to 285 marks.
Farmgate bread wheat prices were around 240-270 marks.
Brokers said harvest progress would decide whether trade and co-op sellers will achieve desired levels especially if competitive British bread wheat offers were to emerge.
Feed wheat markets already eased under British and Danish import pressure. Deals were struck at 250-275 marks a tonne for 1996 dates cif north Germany and above 280 marks for 1997.
Hamburg's grain exchange quoted 277.50 marks free Hamburg for local feed wheat with first-half 1997 at 287.50.
Local feed wheat was supported by harvest reports from eastern Germany showing unsatisfactory barley and wheat yields.
Problems with low falling numbers in rye affected northern Germany to a lesser extent than other regions.
Rainfall has not been as frequent and damaging to rye here as further south, where much of the rye crop will not qualify as bread flour and will add to feed grain supply.
Fob Baltic prices of bread wheat for September-November delivery (250 Hagberg) rose by up to five marks on the week and stood in a 280-310 mark range, depending on lot sizes and protein contents.
Spot export barley was at 250-260 marks, bread rye just under 360 marks and feed rye at 245 marks. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
